leaseTables.finding: atoms_writer_lease_v2 and atoms_bulk_writer_lease are both EMPTY (0 rows) right now. This is structural, not a coincidence of timing: releaseScopedLease (packages/storage/src/atoms-writer-lease.ts) issues DELETE FROM atoms_writer_lease_v2 WHERE holder_token = ... on release, and the table is a live mutex keyed on (scope_type, scope_id) with ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE -- it can only ever show the CURRENT holder of a scope, never a past one. This table cannot corroborate or refute who held the building-footprint/48021 or building-footprint/48453 lease on 2026-09-07; the record was deleted the moment the run finished. This is a real, load-bearing gap: the mission asked for lease rows in the window and none can exist by design, for any past run, not just this one.

writerRunIdContract.finding: APPLY_LEASE_MESSAGE states the writer's own design intent: '--apply requires --run-id (a Factory runs row).' refuseApplyWithoutRunId only checks the flag is a non-empty string; it never validates the value against runs.id (a gen_random_uuid() UUID in the Factory database). The run-ids actually used (bfoot-apply-<fips>-<ISO8601>Z, a human-readable label, not a UUID) do not and structurally cannot match any row in the Factory runs table -- confirmed empty for this purpose in factoryRunsTable above. Separately, holder_label in railLeaseArgs falls back to a hardcoded literal ('building-footprint-writer') unless CLOUD_RUN_EXECUTION or K_REVISION is set in the environment -- both Cloud-Run-only env vars this audit's Cloud Logging read (above) already shows were not in play for this write. So even had the lease row survived, its holder_label would carry no machine- or session-identifying information for a non-Cloud-Run invocation.
writerRunIdContract.significance: This is the root mechanism that makes the write unattributable through the system's own designed channel: the gate that requires a run-id exists, but (a) does not enforce that the id refers to a real Factory run, and (b) discards the id on lease release regardless. The control the writer's own code comment describes was never wired end to end.
